signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Risk + Strait of Hormuz Escalation
signals.text: Trump's declaration of intent to claim the Strait of Hormuz as U.S. territory alongside projectile strikes on a bulk carrier drives an immediate safe-haven bid for the JPY. Despite a +264bp OIS carry advantage for USD, the JPY COT short position of -59.5k (pctl 73) faces squeeze risk as volatility rises from the Friday close of 159.27. Geopolitical escalation typically triggers JPY repatriation, overriding the 1.51% US real rate restrictive advantage. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY into the Sydney open; safe-haven demand outweighs carry. Catalyst: Sydney/Tokyo market open on 16 Aug. Risk: De-escalation headlines or a sudden rise in US 10Y yields above 4.75%.
evidence: Trump headline: Hormuz as US territory
UKMTO report: Bulk carrier hit by projectile

signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: CAD emerges as the G10 leader with a 1W average of +1.052% while JPY lags at -0.974%, creating a strong bilateral spread of 2.026%. The CAD/JPY pair is supported by a +125bp carry advantage and a positive ESI of +10.3, though safe-haven JPY demand following weekend geopolitical events is likely to test this trend. Leveraged funds are net short CAD -92.4k (pctl 12), suggesting any further CAD outperformance is likely to trigger a violent short-covering rally. Trade bias: Bullish CAD/JPY on a 1W momentum basis; divergence in data surprises supports CAD. Catalyst: Sydney/Tokyo open on 16 Aug. Risk: Broad risk-off sentiment favoring JPY safe-haven flows due to Hormuz escalation.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning Risk + Contrarian Sentiment
signals.text: AUD COT LF net long +45.7k (74.6% long) sits at a 75th percentile, creating a crowded-long risk as AUD/USD closed Friday at 0.7092. Retail sentiment is extremely short at 80%, providing a contrarian bid, but the -11.1 ESI indicates domestic data is failing to meet expectations. The 73bp OIS carry advantage for AUD provides a buffer, but the pair's position above all major SMAs leaves it vulnerable to profit-taking. Trade bias: Neutral/Bearish AUD/USD; crowded spec longs and poor economic surprises cap upside. Catalyst: Sydney open on 16 Aug. Risk: Sudden hawkish shift in RBA expectations or a break above the SMA200 at 0.6939 reinforcing momentum.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Crowded Longs + Hedging Demand
signals.text: GBP COT LF net long +42.7k (pctl 90, z=+1.23) represents an extreme bullish consensus that creates significant downside risk if momentum stalls at 1.3533. Elevated options hedging demand is visible in the GBP/USD VRP of +5.0% (IV 11.0% vs HV30 6.0%), suggesting professionals are paying a high premium for protection against a GBP pullback. While the +1.15% real rate is restrictive, the 75% retail short bias warns that the path of least resistance remains higher until speculative longs liquidate. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD; extreme COT positioning and high VRP signal a potential exhaustion point. Catalyst: Sydney open on 16 Aug. Risk: UK inflation data beat or continued DXY weakness toward the 99.17 SMA200 level.

signals.title: NZD/USD — Carry Compression
signals.text: NZD/USD closed at 0.5891 with the RBNZ holds at 2.5%. Speculative positioning is extremely short at -34.0k (pctl 2, z=-2.00), which sets up a massive short-squeeze potential if the Sept 2nd meeting delivers a hawkish outcome. Positive ESI (+9.6) confirms that New Zealand data is outperforming, providing a fundamental floor against the 125bp USD carry advantage. Trade bias: Bullish NZD/USD; extreme COT shorts and positive data surprises favor a squeeze higher. Catalyst: next RBNZ meeting (mkt: 85% hike priced) on 2 Sep. Risk: Broad USD strength driven by a failure of the DXY to break below 99.64.
